tools.description: Create a new GitHub pull request to propose code changes. Use this after making file edits to submit them for review and merging. The PR will be created from the current branch with your committed changes. This is a write-once declaration for a real intended PR, not a sandbox or probe: do not call it with placeholder content, test titles/bodies, or auth experiments. If you are not ready to open the real PR, use noop or report_incomplete instead. For code review comments on an existing PR, use create_pull_request_review_comment instead. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 1 pull request(s) can be created. Title will be prefixed with "[implementer] ". Labels ["agent"] will be automatically added. This tool records a real pull request intent. Do not use it for tests, auth checks, or probing. Call it once only when the final PR title/body/branch are ready; otherwise use noop or report_incomplete.

base.description: Target base branch for the pull request. This override is only allowed when workflow configuration sets safe-outputs.create-pull-request.allowed-base-branches and the value matches one of those patterns, or when it names the branch of a pull request created earlier in the same run (a stacked pull request). Stacked pull requests are rejected when safe-outputs.create-pull-request.stacked is false.

body.description: Detailed PR description in Markdown. Include what changes were made, why, testing notes, and any breaking changes. Do NOT repeat the title as a heading.

branch.description: Source branch name containing the changes. If omitted, uses the current working branch. If the workflow configuration sets safe-outputs.create-pull-request.allowed-branches, then the branch name MUST be given and match one of these patterns.

dependencies.description: Optional list of branch names this pull request depends on (branches of earlier pull requests in the same stack). Used to detect circular stack dependencies and to record stack metadata.

draft.description: Whether to create the PR as a draft. Draft PRs cannot be merged until marked as ready for review. Use mark_pull_request_as_ready_for_review to convert a draft PR. Default: true.

integrity.description: Trustworthiness level of the message source (e.g., "low", "medium", "high").

labels.description: Labels to categorize the PR (e.g., 'enhancement', 'bugfix'). Labels must exist in the repository.

repo.description: Target repository in 'owner/repo' format. For multi-repo workflows where the target repo differs from the workflow repo, this must match a repo in the allowed-repos list or the configured target-repo. If omitted, defaults to the configured target-repo (from safe-outputs config), NOT the workflow repository. In most cases, you should omit this parameter and let the system use the configured default.

secrecy.description: Confidentiality level of the message content (e.g., "public", "internal", "private").

stack_position.description: Optional 1-based position of this pull request within a stack of dependent pull requests. Recorded in the pull request body as stack metadata.

stack_root.description: Optional branch name of the root of the pull request stack (the branch the first pull request in the stack targets). Recorded in the pull request body as stack metadata.

temporary_id.description: Unique temporary identifier for this pull request. Canonical form: '#aw_' followed by 3 to 12 alphanumeric or underscore characters (A-Za-z0-9_) — e.g., '#aw_pr1', '#aw_fix_123'. The bare 'aw_pr1' form is also accepted and normalised to '#aw_pr1'. Use this same '#aw_ID' form in body text to cross-reference this PR; these references are replaced with the real pull request number after creation.

title.description: Concise PR title describing the changes. Follow repository conventions (e.g., conventional commits). The title appears as the main heading.

tools.name: create_pull_request

tools.description: Report that a tool or capability needed to complete the task is not available, or share any information you deem important about missing functionality or limitations. Use this when you cannot accomplish what was requested because the required functionality is missing or access is restricted. When a bash command is blocked by security policy, call this tool with reason set to "security".

alternatives.description: Any workarounds, manual steps, or alternative approaches the user could take (max 256 characters).

integrity.description: Trustworthiness level of the message source (e.g., "low", "medium", "high").

reason.description: Explanation of why this tool is needed or what information you want to share about the limitation (max 256 characters).

secrecy.description: Confidentiality level of the message content (e.g., "public", "internal", "private").

tool.description: Optional: Name or description of the missing tool or capability (max 128 characters). Be specific about what functionality is needed.

tools.name: missing_tool

tools.description: Log a transparency message when no significant actions are needed. Use this to confirm workflow completion and provide visibility when analysis is complete but no changes or outputs are required (e.g., 'No issues found', 'All checks passed'). This ensures the workflow produces human-visible output even when no other actions are taken.

integrity.description: Trustworthiness level of the message source (e.g., "low", "medium", "high").

message.description: Status or completion message to log. Should explain what was analyzed and the outcome (e.g., 'Code review complete - no issues found', 'Analysis complete - all tests passing'). This is the only content field noop accepts; common aliases (reason, summary, details, text, note, status) are accepted and mapped to message. Serialize any metrics or structured run summary into this single string; other named fields (for example processed, skipped) are not accepted and cause a missing-message error.

secrecy.description: Confidentiality level of the message content (e.g., "public", "internal", "private").

tools.name: noop

tools.description: Report that data or information needed to complete the task is not available. Use this when you cannot accomplish what was requested because required data, context, or information is missing.

alternatives.description: Any workarounds, manual steps, or alternative approaches the user could take (max 256 characters).

context.description: Additional context about the missing data or where it should come from (max 256 characters).

data_type.description: Type or description of the missing data or information (max 128 characters). Be specific about what data is needed.

integrity.description: Trustworthiness level of the message source (e.g., "low", "medium", "high").

reason.description: Explanation of why this data is needed to complete the task (max 256 characters).

secrecy.description: Confidentiality level of the message content (e.g., "public", "internal", "private").

tools.name: missing_data

tools.description: Signal that the task could not be completed due to an infrastructure or tool failure (e.g., MCP server crash, missing authentication, inaccessible repository). Use this when required tools or data are unavailable and the task cannot be meaningfully performed. This is distinct from noop (no action needed) — it indicates an active failure that prevented the task from running. Provide a specific reason and optional details so downstream issue aggregation can preserve complete incomplete-signal context. The workflow framework will treat this as a failure signal even when the agent exits successfully.

details.description: Optional extended details or diagnostic context about the failure (max 65000 characters).

reason.description: A concise explanation of why the task could not be completed (max 1024 characters). Be specific about which tools or resources were unavailable.

tools.name: report_incomplete
